skill_name: Identity and Access Management (IAM) & Least Privilege
subtopic: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE
question_text: [Identity and Access Management (IAM) & Least Privilege - Q24] What security threat does Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) mitigate in public OAuth 2.0 clients (mobile and single-page apps)?

options.text: Authorization Code Interception attacks where malicious apps on the device intercept the authorization code returned by the browser custom URI scheme
DDoS attacks on the authorization server
Brute force attacks on user passwords

answer_explanation: Public clients cannot securely store a `client_secret`. PKCE generates a dynamic `code_verifier` and hashed `code_challenge`. The authorization server releases tokens only when the original verifier is presented.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Public clients cannot securely store a `client_secret`. PKCE generates a dynamic `code_verifier` and hashed `code_challenge`. The authorization server releases tokens only when the original verifier is presented.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
